name: 김소월 (Kim So-wol)
bio: A foundational modern Korean lyric poet whose work draws on folk songs and the language of separation.
style: Songlike repetition, plain diction, traditional rhythms, and restrained grief turn absence into intimate lyric drama.

name: 서정주 (Seo Jeong-ju)
bio: A major twentieth-century Korean poet whose writing moves from bodily intensity toward Buddhist and mythic imagination.
style: Lush imagery, incantatory rhythms, folklore, and Buddhist reflection give ordinary life a mythic scale.

name: 정지용 (Jeong Ji-yong)
bio: A pioneering Korean modernist who refined the sensory language of modern Korean poetry.
style: Precise visual and aural images, controlled musicality, and sharply observed landscapes carry longing without excessive explanation.

name: 김수영 (Kim Su-yeong)
bio: A Korean modernist and advocate of poetic freedom whose work engages everyday life and political oppression.
style: Conversational free verse, abrupt turns, irony, and stubborn physical images link private unease to demands for freedom.

name: 백석 (Baek Seok)
bio: A Korean poet celebrated for preserving northern regional speech, food, customs, and communal memory.
style: Dialect, sensory detail, long rhythmic sentences, and remembered village life create a warm but displaced world.

name: 한용운 (Han Yong-un)
bio: A Buddhist monk, poet, and independence activist who joined spiritual inquiry with the struggle against colonial rule.
style: Paradox, devotional address, and meditative prose rhythms allow the absent beloved to suggest love, liberation, and enlightenment.

name: 김춘수 (Kim Chun-su)
bio: A Korean poet known for exploring naming, existence, and a poetics that loosens ordinary meaning.
style: Clear images and repeated phrases move from philosophical lyricism toward associative, meaning-resistant sequences.

name: 이상 (Yi Sang)
bio: An architect and experimental writer central to the Korean literary avant-garde of the colonial period.
style: Numerals, fractured syntax, spatial arrangements, and unsettling repetitions turn the modern self into a psychological puzzle.

name: 박목월 (Park Mok-wol)
bio: A Korean lyric poet and member of the Cheongnok group, known for imagined rural landscapes.
style: Sparse musical lines, folk rhythms, and softened natural images create distance, quiet longing, and pastoral calm.

name: 윤동주 (Yun Dong-ju)
bio: A Korean poet of conscience who died in Japanese imprisonment before his first collection appeared.
style: Plain, prayerlike language and images of stars, sky, and roads frame self-examination, shame, hope, and responsibility.

name: 김영랑 (Kim Yeong-nang)
bio: A Korean lyric poet associated with the Simunhak circle and the musical possibilities of Korean speech.
style: Delicate sound patterns, southern vernacular, and concentrated flower imagery balance radiant beauty with sorrow.

name: 이육사 (Yi Yuk-sa)
bio: A Korean independence activist and poet who repeatedly endured imprisonment under Japanese colonial rule.
style: Firm declarative lines, vast landscapes, and prophetic images express endurance, moral resolve, and a future beyond oppression.

name: 박인환 (Park In-hwan)
bio: A postwar Korean modernist whose poems register the dislocation and melancholy of urban life.
style: Cosmopolitan references, drifting urban images, elegiac speech, and romantic disillusion evoke a damaged postwar world.

name: 김광균 (Kim Gwang-gyun)
bio: A Korean modernist noted for developing a pictorial approach to poetry and the modern city.
style: Visual composition, color, lamplight, and urban scenery make loneliness visible through carefully arranged images.

name: 김현승 (Kim Hyeon-seung)
bio: A Korean poet whose Christian upbringing shaped a lifelong inquiry into solitude, faith, and human limits.
style: Austere language, autumnal images, and reflective address transform loneliness into spiritual and ethical questioning.

name: 노천명 (No Cheon-myeong)
bio: A Korean poet and journalist known for lyrics of solitude and a proud, inward sensibility.
style: Restrained confession, clear natural images, and a reserved voice give loneliness and wounded dignity a precise shape.

name: 고은 (Ko Un)
bio: A prolific Korean poet whose work ranges from Buddhist-inflected lyrics to portraits of ordinary people.
style: Rapid shifts between spare insight and expansive storytelling animate remembered lives, landscapes, and collective history.

name: 신경림 (Shin Gyeong-nim)
bio: A Korean poet who brought rural workers, folk culture, and communal struggle into modern lyric poetry.
style: Folk-song rhythms, plainspoken narrative, and collective voices give rural labor, hardship, and solidarity bodily force.

name: 김남조 (Kim Nam-jo)
bio: A Korean poet and educator known for poetry of love, Christian faith, and human solidarity.
style: Warm direct address, prayerlike cadences, and images of light and warmth shape an affirmative yet suffering-aware lyric voice.

name: 김지하 (Kim Ji-ha)
bio: A Korean poet and dissident whose satire became closely associated with resistance to authoritarian rule.
style: Pansori-like momentum, biting satire, vernacular energy, and public address expose injustice with dramatic force.

name: 신동엽 (Shin Dong-yeop)
bio: A Korean poet whose work connects national division, popular resistance, and the hope for renewal.
style: Urgent repetition, earthy images, and historical vision strip away false appearances in search of communal dignity.

name: 박재삼 (Park Jae-sam)
bio: A Korean lyric poet who wrote of poverty, childhood, love, and the emotional inheritance of ordinary lives.
style: Traditional cadence, southern speech, and river or sea imagery hold grief within a clear, singing surface.

name: 조지훈 (Jo Ji-hun)
bio: A poet, scholar, and member of the Cheongnok group who explored Korean cultural traditions.
style: Classical poise, measured musicality, and carefully staged movement join aesthetic beauty to historical and spiritual depth.

name: 박두진 (Park Du-jin)
bio: A Korean poet of the Cheongnok group whose nature poetry often carries Christian and historical aspirations.
style: Exclamatory rhythms, vivid mountains and sunlight, and a prophetic voice turn nature into a promise of renewal.

name: 정호승 (Jeong Ho-seung)
bio: A Korean poet whose accessible lyrics attend to loneliness, suffering, and the possibility of consolation.
style: Simple direct speech, familiar images, and compassionate reversals allow sorrow to become a source of fellowship.

name: 안도현 (An Do-hyeon)
bio: A Korean poet and teacher known for finding moral and emotional significance in humble things.
style: Conversational brevity, personified objects, and close attention to everyday labor open into quiet ethical questions.

name: 김용택 (Kim Yong-taek)
bio: A Korean poet and former village schoolteacher whose work is rooted in the Seomjin River region.
style: Unadorned rural speech, close observation, and river landscapes join personal affection to the lives of neighbors.

name: 도종환 (Do Jong-hwan)
bio: A Korean poet, former teacher, and politician whose early elegies address the loss of his wife.
style: Accessible diction, seasonal flowers, and patient repetition join intimate mourning to endurance and social concern.

name: 나태주 (Na Tae-ju)
bio: A Korean poet and former elementary-school teacher known for brief lyrics that invite attentive affection.
style: Short plainspoken lines, small natural subjects, and gentle turns of perception make tenderness feel immediate.

name: 문정희 (Moon Jeong-hee)
bio: A Korean poet whose work asserts female experience, bodily vitality, and independence.
style: Bold direct address, sensuous bodily images, and energetic irony challenge prescribed roles and celebrate desire.

name: 황동규 (Hwang Dong-gyu)
bio: A Korean poet and scholar of English literature known for reflective lyrics and extended poetic journeys.
style: Shifting perspectives, conversational movement, and exact landscape details let travel and memory become philosophical discovery.

name: 기형도 (Ki Hyung-do)
bio: A Korean poet and journalist whose posthumous first collection became a landmark of urban alienation.
style: Shadowed city scenes, anxious narrative, and dreamlike dislocations create a haunted atmosphere of loss and isolation.

name: 정현종 (Jung Hyun-jong)
bio: A Korean poet and educator whose writing explores presence, relationship, and the vitality of being.
style: Airy brevity, lively metaphor, and sudden philosophical turns celebrate the depth of encounters and the freedom of things.

name: 오규원 (O Gyu-won)
bio: A Korean experimental poet and teacher who developed an approach centered on immediate perception.
style: Precise visual relations, stripped language, and minimal explanation let things appear before familiar judgments settle on them.

name: 이성복 (Lee Seong-bok)
bio: A Korean poet and scholar of French literature whose work confronts damaged relationships and historical suffering.
style: Jarring juxtapositions, intimate address, and scenes of bodily vulnerability make private pain disclose a wider fractured world.

name: 황지우 (Hwang Ji-wu)
bio: A Korean poet and artist whose experiments engage authoritarianism, mass culture, and everyday perception.
style: Collage, typography, found language, and abrupt tonal changes interrupt ordinary scenes with political and existential pressure.

name: 최승자 (Choi Seung-ja)
bio: A Korean poet and translator whose unsparing lyrics transformed the language of alienation and female subjectivity.
style: Blunt confession, corrosive irony, bodily imagery, and emotional extremes give loneliness an uncompromising voice.

name: 구상 (Ku Sang)
bio: A Korean poet and journalist whose work reflects on war, faith, and ethical responsibility.
style: Plain narrative, biblical resonance, and meditative attention to daily life connect historical suffering with spiritual accountability.

name: 허영자 (Heo Yeong-ja)
bio: A Korean poet and educator known for compressed lyrics of love, sorrow, and spiritual reflection.
style: Restrained diction, compact musical form, and images of craft and nature contain intense feeling within careful limits.

name: 이근배 (Lee Geun-bae)
bio: A Korean poet who has worked in both free verse and the traditional sijo form.
style: Polished cadence, tactile cultural images, and concentrated lyric turns connect personal feeling with historical memory.

name: 김종해 (Kim Jong-hae)
bio: A Korean poet and publisher whose writing moves between modernist unease and resilient human warmth.
style: Surreal combinations, sea imagery, and a searching lyric voice turn adversity toward freedom and renewal.

name: 이건청 (Lee Geon-cheong)
bio: A Korean poet and educator whose writing brings inward lyric reflection into contact with ecological and prehistoric worlds.
style: Concrete natural images, reflective narrative, and deep historical perspectives explore endangered life and the self.

name: 오세영 (O Se-yeong)
bio: A Korean poet and literary scholar whose work investigates desire, existence, and Buddhist thought.
style: Controlled lyric form, paradox, and recurring natural symbols give existential questions a lucid, meditative shape.

name: 신달자 (Shin Dal-ja)
bio: A Korean poet and essayist whose writing explores womanhood, family, bereavement, and renewal.
style: Candid emotional speech, tactile domestic details, and images of endurance turn personal wounds toward compassion.

name: 최동호 (Choi Dong-ho)
bio: A Korean poet, critic, and educator whose work joins contemplative lyricism with attention to living things.
style: Compressed images, Buddhist-inflected reflection, and close observation seek flashes of life within ordinary objects.

name: 유자효 (Yu Ja-hyo)
bio: A Korean poet and broadcaster whose lyric work reflects on love, memory, and human vulnerability.
style: Clear musical language, restrained sorrow, and familiar scenes build intimate reflections on attachment and passing time.

name: 유안진 (Yu An-jin)
bio: A Korean poet, essayist, and scholar whose writing spans lyric poetry and reflections on relationships.
style: Supple musical phrasing, intimate address, and symbolic natural images carry longing, friendship, and self-discovery.

name: 김광규 (Kim Kwang-gyu)
bio: A Korean poet and German-literature scholar known for exposing social habits through ordinary language.
style: Plain narrative, everyday scenes, and understated irony reveal conformity, compromised ideals, and the absurdities of modern life.

name: 마종기 (Ma Jong-gi)
bio: A Korean poet and physician whose writing draws on medicine, migration, and the fragility of life.
style: Quiet conversational lines, bodily observation, and restrained tenderness connect mortality with memory and distant attachments.

name: 오상순 (O Sang-sun)
bio: An early modern Korean poet associated with the literary journal Pyeheo and a life of wandering.
style: Expansive contemplation, images of wandering, and a tension between emptiness and cosmic vitality shape a searching voice.

name: 김동환 (Kim Dong-hwan)
bio: A Korean poet and editor who helped establish the modern Korean narrative poem.
style: Broad narrative movement, northern landscapes, and folk-inflected rhythms make individual hardship part of a larger social scene.

name: 김종삼 (Kim Jong-sam)
bio: A Korean poet known for spare, elliptical poems shaped by music, art, and memories of war.
style: Omission, broken transitions, and small luminous scenes suggest an inaccessible world of beauty beyond deprivation.

name: 김혜순 (Kim Hye-soon)
bio: A Korean poet and essayist whose experimental work explores the female body, death, and collective trauma.
style: Surreal bodily transformations, polyphonic voices, and unsettling humor dismantle stable identities and conventional lyric speech.

name: 황인숙 (Hwang In-suk)
bio: A Korean poet whose writing pays close attention to city streets, solitude, and overlooked lives.
style: Conversational agility, sudden humor, and quick urban images turn vulnerability and affection into restless lyric movement.

name: 강은교 (Kang Eun-gyo)
bio: A Korean poet and educator whose work connects mortality, emptiness, and the bonds among living beings.
style: Incantatory repetition, spare visionary images, and collective voices move between existential desolation and solidarity.

name: 곽재구 (Kwak Jae-gu)
bio: A Korean poet known for lyrical portraits of ordinary people and marginalized places.
style: Warm narrative, sensory local detail, and a measured elegiac rhythm discover dignity in waiting, labor, and small communities.

name: 이성부 (Lee Seong-bu)
bio: A Korean poet whose work joins social commitment with an enduring attention to mountains and walking.
style: Earthy diction, strong natural images, and patient physical movement express collective endurance and ethical determination.

name: 천양희 (Cheon Yang-hui)
bio: A Korean poet whose writing transforms isolation and suffering into intense acts of perception.
style: Concentrated images, forceful internal rhythms, and searching questions turn private anguish into attention to the wider world.

name: 허수경 (Heo Su-gyeong)
bio: A Korean poet and archaeologist who lived in Germany and wrote of exile, memory, and historical wounds.
style: Earthy southern speech, bodily images, and intimate address make distance and dispossession feel physically present.

name: 나희덕 (Na Hee-deok)
bio: A Korean poet and educator whose work closely observes growth, vulnerability, and relationships.
style: Restrained musical language, plant imagery, and attentive shifts of perspective give ordinary life ethical and emotional depth.

name: 최영미 (Choi Yeong-mi)
bio: A Korean poet and novelist whose first collection examined disillusionment after the political struggles of the 1980s.
style: Direct colloquial speech, sharp irony, and frank accounts of desire and disappointment question public ideals and private compromises.

name: 이문재 (Lee Mun-jae)
bio: A Korean poet and journalist whose work considers modern speed, ecological damage, and the practice of attention.
style: Walking rhythms, reflective questions, and ordinary landscapes slow perception and expose the pressures of contemporary life.

name: 문태준 (Moon Tae-jun)
bio: A Korean poet whose work brings rural memory and Buddhist sensibility into contemporary lyric poetry.
style: Quiet precise images, patient observation, and gentle associations reveal shared vulnerability among people and other living beings.

name: 손택수 (Son Taek-su)
bio: A Korean poet whose writing connects rural childhood, urban displacement, and working lives.
style: Tactile images, supple vernacular, and unexpected transformations connect family memory with animals, plants, and labor.

name: 김기택 (Kim Ki-taek)
bio: A Korean poet known for closely examining bodies, animals, and the pressures of routine urban existence.
style: Microscopic observation, unsettling bodily detail, and dry irony expose violence and constraint inside familiar movements.

name: 이승훈 (Lee Seung-hun)
bio: A Korean experimental poet and critic who questioned the stability of language, objects, and the poetic self.
style: Fragmentation, repetition, and self-questioning language unsettle ordinary categories and blur the boundary between poetry and daily life.

name: 김종길 (Kim Jong-gil)
bio: A Korean poet and English-literature scholar known for exact, restrained lyric craft.
style: Clear sensory detail, disciplined cadence, and emotionally measured recollection let concrete scenes carry affection and loss.

name: 송찬호 (Song Chan-ho)
bio: A Korean poet whose work develops an imaginative world of animals, objects, and transformed landscapes.
style: Surreal metamorphosis, fablelike movement, and playful verbal precision make the familiar uncanny and newly visible.

name: 문인수 (Moon In-su)
bio: A Korean poet whose late literary debut preceded sustained writing about ordinary people, loss, and endurance.
style: Spare conversational lines, sharply caught gestures, and sudden emotional turns find large griefs in small daily events.

name: 하종오 (Ha Jong-o)
bio: A Korean poet whose work has addressed rural life, historical violence, and the experiences of migrants.
style: Plain narrative, concrete labor scenes, and shifting social perspectives insist on the dignity of excluded people.

name: 이재무 (Lee Jae-mu)
bio: A Korean poet and educator whose writing attends to rural memory and the friction of everyday life.
style: Earthy diction, sensuous observation, and colloquial turns make ordinary objects reveal desire, hardship, and stubborn vitality.

name: 심보선 (Shim Bo-seon)
bio: A Korean poet and sociologist whose writing investigates loneliness, community, and the possibility of human connection.
style: Conversational reasoning, ironic detours, and unexpected tenderness bring philosophical questions into ordinary encounters.

name: 김소연 (Kim So-yeon)
bio: A Korean poet and essayist known for precise language about intimacy, memory, and estrangement.
style: Careful verbal distinctions, spare images, and oblique address reveal the distances hidden inside familiar relationships.

name: 김경주 (Kim Gyeong-ju)
bio: A Korean poet and playwright whose work moves across poetry, performance, and theatrical language.
style: Dreamlike leaps, unstable speakers, and intense sensory associations create a restless world of displacement and impossible encounters.

name: 이병률 (Lee Byeong-ryul)
bio: A Korean poet and travel essayist whose work explores solitude, movement, and fleeting relationships.
style: Intimate address, spare travel images, and emotional ellipsis make departure and chance encounters resonate with longing.

name: 박형준 (Park Hyeong-jun)
bio: A Korean poet and educator whose writing reflects on childhood, poverty, and the persistence of memory.
style: Delicate sensory images, quiet narrative, and attention to fading traces make absence and memory physically palpable.

name: 장석남 (Jang Seok-nam)
bio: A Korean poet whose work renews lyric poetry through intimate observations and musical association.
style: Fluid images, subtle rhythm, and unexpected links among ordinary things create quiet wonder and emotional depth.

name: 김상용 (Kim Sang-yong)
bio: A Korean poet, translator, and scholar of English literature known for restrained pastoral lyrics.
style: Plain balanced phrasing, modest rural scenes, and understated humor suggest contentment beyond worldly ambition.

name: 주요한 (Ju Yo-han)
bio: An early modern Korean poet, journalist, and politician who helped introduce new forms of vernacular poetry.
style: Sensory intensity, emotional directness, and flexible prose-poem rhythms break from inherited poetic conventions.

name: 김동명 (Kim Dong-myeong)
bio: A Korean poet and essayist whose lyrics frequently join natural imagery to longing and inward feeling.
style: Songlike repetition, direct metaphor, and lucid natural symbols give private emotion a readily memorable form.

name: 조병화 (Jo Byeong-hwa)
bio: A Korean poet and educator whose prolific lyric writing reflects on solitude, love, and transience.
style: Accessible speech, recurring images of clouds and journeys, and gentle reflection make loneliness a companion of daily life.

name: 박남수 (Park Nam-su)
bio: A Korean poet who experienced national division and later emigrated to the United States.
style: Exact visual images, compressed language, and symbolic birds or light investigate perception, freedom, and the limits of innocence.

name: 김달진 (Kim Dal-jin)
bio: A Korean poet and translator of classical Chinese and Buddhist texts whose poetry seeks contemplative clarity.
style: Quiet natural observation, spare imagery, and Buddhist and Daoist reflection dissolve the division between observer and world.

name: 이형기 (Lee Hyeong-gi)
bio: A Korean poet and critic whose work moved from traditional lyricism toward darker experimental forms.
style: Controlled lyric cadence gives way to grotesque images and irony, while transience and self-erasure remain recurring concerns.

name: 정철 (Jeong Cheol)
bio: A Joseon statesman and poet celebrated for long vernacular gasa and sijo.
style: Rolling gasa rhythms, richly staged landscapes, and courtly address combine personal feeling with political and moral aspiration.

name: 윤선도 (Yun Seon-do)
bio: A Joseon scholar, official, and poet whose sijo cycles explore life among mountains, rivers, and the sea.
style: Seasonal structure, recurring refrains, and precise natural images give withdrawal from public life a buoyant musical form.

name: 황진이 (Hwang Jin-i)
bio: A sixteenth-century gisaeng and poet remembered for exceptional literary skill and sijo of desire and separation.
style: Compressed three-part movement, ingenious metaphor, and poised wit give longing and emotional independence memorable shape.

name: 허난설헌 (Heo Nan-seol-heon)
bio: A sixteenth-century Joseon poet whose classical Chinese verse gained readership beyond Korea after her death.
style: Refined classical imagery, imagined immortal realms, and intimate laments express frustrated talent, grief, and longing.

name: 박인로 (Park In-no)
bio: A Joseon soldier and poet known for gasa that explore duty, poverty, and rural life.
style: Extended vernacular rhythms, concrete rustic details, and Confucian reflection bring material hardship into sustained moral inquiry.

name: 송순 (Song Sun)
bio: A Joseon official and poet whose retirement landscape became the setting for influential gasa.
style: Flowing catalogues of scenery, balanced seasonal images, and a spacious viewpoint celebrate cultivated life in nature.

name: 이황 (Yi Hwang)
bio: A Joseon Neo-Confucian philosopher and educator whose poetry unites learning with life in nature.
style: Ordered sijo sequences, mountain-and-stream imagery, and quiet exhortation connect self-cultivation with attentive perception.

name: 이이 (Yi I)
bio: A Joseon Neo-Confucian philosopher and statesman whose sijo also explore scholarly life in the landscape.
style: Structured landscape sequences, clear seasonal images, and measured moral reflection make nature a setting for learning.

name: 정몽주 (Jeong Mong-ju)
bio: A late Goryeo scholar and diplomat remembered for loyalty to the dynasty and his assassination during its fall.
style: Compact sijo argument, emphatic repetition, and images of bodily destruction express unwavering ethical resolve.

name: 김삿갓 (Kim Sat-gat)
bio: The pen name of Kim Byeong-yeon, a wandering nineteenth-century poet famed for satirical classical Chinese verse.
style: Puns, double meanings, sharp reversals, and irreverent social observation expose pretension and delight in verbal surprise.

name: 정약용 (Jeong Yak-yong)
bio: A Joseon scholar of practical learning and official whose poetry records exile, poverty, and social injustice.
style: Concrete narrative, compassionate observation, and classical discipline turn individual suffering into a critique of unjust institutions.

name: 이색 (Yi Saek)
bio: A late Goryeo scholar, educator, and poet who helped transmit Neo-Confucian learning.
style: Classical Chinese forms, historical reflection, and restrained landscape observation join scholarly discipline with dynastic melancholy.

name: 김천택 (Kim Cheon-taek)
bio: A Joseon singer, sijo poet, and compiler whose anthology helped preserve the Korean song tradition.
style: Balanced sijo phrasing, conversational wit, and natural images make song a vehicle for feeling and social observation.

name: 성삼문 (Seong Sam-mun)
bio: A Joseon scholar and poet executed after an attempt to restore the deposed King Danjong.
style: Compact sijo structure, steadfast declarative speech, and resilient natural symbols make loyalty the organizing emotional force.

name: 김시습 (Kim Si-seup)
bio: A Joseon poet, scholar, and Buddhist monk who lived outside official service after King Sejo seized the throne.
style: Classical Chinese verse, wandering landscapes, Buddhist reflection, and moral unease express an independent, unsettled spirit.

name: 윤석산 (Yun Seok-san)
bio: A Korean poet and scholar of Donghak and Cheondoism whose work revisits folklore and ordinary urban lives.
style: Reimagined traditional figures, reflective everyday scenes, and compassionate attention to overlooked people join historical memory with daily experience.
